title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is sheet (2) of a short dossier titled 'Question des lims filtrantes dans Hot', written around 1982. The next sheet is a computer job log dated 4 June 1982. The question is whether filtering (direct) colimits exist in the homotopy category Hot = Hot(W). It also asks whether the canonical functors Cat -> Hot(W) and A^ -> Hot_A ≃ Hot(W) commute with them, where A is a test category, A^ = presheaves on A, and Hot_A = A^[W_A^{-1}].

Step 1 (reduction to presheaves). The Cat case reduces to the case A = Δ. The standard test functor i: Δ -> Cat, [n] |-> the ordered set [n], gives the nerve i^*: Cat -> Δ^. The nerve commutes with filtering colimits because each i(a) is a finitely presented object of Cat.

Step 2 (countable case). It suffices to treat an N-indexed system X_0 -> X_1 -> X_2 -> ... in A^. Factor each composite as a monomorphism followed by a weak equivalence ('homotopism'). Inductively this gives a tower X'_0 ↪ X'_1 ↪ X'_2 ↪ ... with all maps mono. It maps to the original tower by weak equivalences u_i, with u_0 = id. Let X'_∞ and X_∞ be the colimits in A^, with induced map u_∞.

Two things must be checked:
(i) X'_∞ is the colimit of the X'_i in Hot_A, i.e. Hot_A has countable filtering colimits of mono-towers and A^ -> Hot_A preserves them.
(ii) u_∞ is an isomorphism in Hot_A, indeed a weak equivalence.
Granting (i), (ii) is equivalent to the full commutation statement for countable filtering colimits.

Step 3. He begins to verify the universal property (*): Hom_Hot(X_∞, Y) -> lim_i Hom_Hot(X_i, Y) should be bijective. The page ends here, and the following sheet is a job log, so the thread stops.

The mono replacement is the classical telescope / homotopy-colimit construction. Grothendieck is in effect testing whether the homotopy colimit is a genuine categorical colimit in Hot.
errors: The hoped-for property (*) is false in general. For a sequential homotopy colimit, Milnor's sequence 0 -> lim^1 [ΣX_i, Y] -> [hocolim X_i, Y] -> lim [X_i, Y] -> 0 shows the map is surjective but not injective. Phantom maps give nonzero kernel. So X'_∞ is only a weak colimit in Hot, and (i) fails as stated. Genuine sequential/filtered colimits do not exist in Hot in general. Grothendieck's own '(?)' signals the doubt, and the issue is not resolved on this page.

Point (ii) is correct, but the mono replacement is not needed for it. Weak equivalences in Δ^ (and W_A for a test category, via A/colim X_i = colim A/X_i and stability of W_Cat under filtered colimits) are already stable under filtered colimits. The monos matter only for identifying the strict colimit with the homotopy colimit.

missed.claim: Grothendieck started checking whether the strict colimit of a mono-tower is a genuine colimit in Hot, and abandoned the computation mid-sentence. The known answer is negative (lim^1 / phantom maps). This is an early (c. 1982) instance of the observation that motivates derivators, but nothing new to specialists.
missed.quote: To check the limiting property (*) Hom_Hot(X_∞, Y) ⥲ lim Hom_Hot(X_i, Y)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only historically: it documents a pre-Pursuing-Stacks moment where Grothendieck is meeting the weak-colimit problem in Hot, which he later addressed via derivators.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine homotopy-theory reasoning (telescope, nerve and filtered colimits). The central hoped-for claim is false in general (lim^1), and the thread breaks off. The only interest is historical, as an early trace of the derivator motivation.
transcription_corrections: Title line: 'Filtering lims exist in (Hot)?' – the word is 'lims' (limits), underlined.
'factorisation of any morphism as pr. with i mono and a homotopism' should read roughly 'as p·i, with i mono and p a homotopism'.
'(ii) ... is an iso in (Hot)_A, i.e. is in W' with the interlinear addition '(weak equivalence, in fact)'.
The '(2)' at top is a circled sheet number; '18' bottom-left is the archive page number.
